title: Attio Review (2026)
intro: Modern, flexible CRM for startups and GTM teams with a data-model-first workspace and AI assistance. This review covers verified 2026 pricing, core CRM capabilities, limitations, and who should buy — based on official first-party sources.
summary: Attio scores reflect first-party research — not hands-on product testing.
verdict: Attio is a strong modern CRM for startups and GTM teams that want flexible data modeling and AI without legacy CRM weight. EUR Free/Plus/Pro pricing is clear; Enterprise is custom. Based on first-party research — not hands-on testing.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Modern data-model-first UI is marketed as approachable for startups; less legacy CRM clutter than Salesforce-class tools.
Flexible lists/pipelines and deal workflows are core to Attio’s CRM story.
Automation is solid for a modern CRM; depth trails specialist engagement suites on lower plans.
Email sync and sequences fit GTM workflows; not a full marketing automation suite.
Reporting is capable for startup/mid-market GTM; enterprise BI buyers may want more.
Flexible objects/attributes and data model are a primary differentiator.
Growing integration surface for modern stacks; ecosystem still younger than Salesforce/HubSpot.
Self-serve Plus/Pro keeps admin lighter than enterprise CRMs; Free→Plus path is simple.
Pro/Enterprise path supports growing GTM orgs; very large enterprises may still compare Salesforce.
Free tier plus clear EUR Plus/Pro pricing is competitive for startups; Pro is premium vs SMB CRMs.

bestFor: Startups and GTM teams wanting flexible CRM
Buyers prioritizing modern UX and data model
notIdealFor: Buyers requiring published USD list prices
cons: Pro pricing is premium vs SMB CRMs
Forecasting depth more limited on lower tiers

limitations: Confirm live Attio checkout; packaging can change.
whoShouldChoose: Choose Attio when it matches your CRM buying criteria above.
whoShouldConsiderAlternatives: Consider alternatives like hubspot, pipedrive, folk if fit is weak.
